claims: The Integrated Public Alert & Warning System (IPAWS) is FEMA's national system.
IPAWS allows federal, state, local, tribal, and territorial authorities to send authenticated emergency messages to the public.
IPAWS simultaneously distributes alerts via mobile phones (Wireless Emergency Alerts), radio/television (Emergency Alert System), and NOAA Weather Radios.
Alerting authorities submit messages using the Common Alerting Protocol (CAP).
CAP messages are disseminated to multiple channels.
IPAWS alerts are sent automatically to cell phones in the targeted area.
No sign-up or opt-in is needed for IPAWS alerts.
Wireless Emergency Alerts (WEA) are text-like messages on mobile phones.
Emergency Alert System (EAS) alerts are broadcast on TV and radio.
NOAA Weather Radio messages are for weather and non-weather events.
Authorized local officials, such as police or emergency management departments, can issue IPAWS alerts.
IPAWS alerts do not rely solely on federal authority.
IPAWS-OPEN is the open platform for emergency networks that validates and authenticates messages.
IPAWS Alerting Authorities are organizations trained and accredited by FEMA to use the system.
IPAWS Alerting Pathways is the communication infrastructure, including cellular carriers, radio, and television stations.
